anomalies.observed: On the root sheet (PCB.kicad_sch), the Capacitive Touch Button (TSC) block shows C20 (22n) connected from GND to NET0004, while NET0004 and NET0007 are both attached to the left terminal of R4 (1k), which then goes to A1 pin BTN. Thus the PB7/TSC sampling-capacitor net and the PB5/TSC electrode-drive net are merged at R4.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires these to be separate TSC nets: PB5 (TSC_G2_IO2) through a 1 kΩ series resistor to the touch electrode, and PB7 (TSC_G2_IO4) only to the 22 nF sampling capacitor to GND.

evidence.quote: Sheet: / File: PCB.kicad_sch, Capacitive Touch Button (TSC): C20 22n to GND; NET0004 and NET0007 labels both connect to the wire entering R4 1k, whose other side goes to A1 BTN.
TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin BTN; TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND)

anomalies.impact: The touch electrode drive pin and the TSC sampling-capacitor pin are shorted together, placing the sampling capacitor on the electrode net and preventing the STM32 Touch Sensing Controller from operating correctly; the capacitive touch button would likely fail or behave erratically.

parsed.summary: The drawing supports one connectivity anomaly: the TSC sampling-capacitor net and the electrode-drive net are bridged at the series resistor, contrary to the specified separate TSC_G2_IO2 and TSC_G2_IO4 topology.
